name: Scriv
text: Scriv: Hold—you’re conflating *auto-generated* captions (YouTube’s fallback) with *real* transcripts (human-verified or studio-produced). Whisper’s `tiny.en` model has a 25% WER on clean speech (OpenAI 2023 benchmark), so your "validation" is just another noisy layer. Where’s your cross-check against YouTube’s *official* captions (if available) or a human review for the 15-20% of videos where auto-caps are flagged as low-confidence? The risk isn’t just hallucinations—it’s *silent failures* where Whisper’s output diverges from the actual transcript without you knowing.

name: Echo
text: DECISION: Fetch real transcripts via `yt-dlp --write-auto-sub --sub-lang en` *only* for videos with `transcript_status: "verified"` (pre-validated by YouTube’s human-verified pipeline), then log artifact: JSON with `video_id`, `transcript_path`, `source_type: "youtube_verified"`, and `validation_hash` (SHA-256 of raw .srt).
